images.filename: StateLibQld 1 209203 Side entrance of Jimbour House, ca. 1928.jpg
images.caption:
Side entrance of Jimbour House, ca. 1928.
Jimbour Station property was one of the largest properties taken up in the 1840s.The pastoral run name was first used by Henry Dennis the pastoralist in 1841. Sanstone blocks for the house were quarried from the area nearby and the tiles were Welsh slate.
images.alt:
Side entrance of Jimbour House, ca. 1928.
Jimbour Station property was one of the largest properties taken up in the 1840s.The pastoral run name was first used by Henry Dennis the pastoralist in 1841. Sanstone blocks for the house were quarried from the area nearby and the tiles were Welsh slate.

images.caption:
O.M.D. Bell and guests in the fernery at Jimbour House, Queensland, ca. 1892
Inscribed on original: ' O.M.D. Bell; Ethel Seymour (father D. T. Seymour); C. S. A.(?) Bell; Eveline Griffith (Sir Samuel Griffith's daughter, now Mrs Tom Brown) . D. T. Seymour was Queensland Commissioner of Police. Eveline Griffith married Thomas Brown in 1894.

images.filename: StateLibQld 1 40199 Guests at Jimbour House pose on the front steps under floodlights, 1925.jpg
images.caption:
Guests at Jimbour House pose on the front steps under floodlights, 1925
On 21 November 1925 Jimbour House was formally re-opened with a fund raising fete for Dalby Hospital. It was held at the end of extensive renovations to the house and garden carried out by the Russell family.
images.alt:
Guests at Jimbour House pose on the front steps under floodlights, 1925
On 21 November 1925 Jimbour House was formally re-opened with a fund raising fete for Dalby Hospital. It was held at the end of extensive renovations to the house and garden carried out by the Russell family.
